aiExplanation: This solves **Stone Game V** with interval dynamic programming. First it builds a `prefix` sum array so the total value of any contiguous slice of stones can be computed in constant time as `prefix[end + 1] - prefix[start]`. Then `dp[left][right]` stores the **maximum score Alice can earn** from the stones between indices `left` and `right`. The code fills this table from shorter ranges to longer ones (`len` from 2 up to `n`), and for each range it tries every possible split point `mid`: the left part is `left..mid` and the right part is `mid + 1..right`. Per the game rules, Bob discards the half with the **larger sum**, Alice scores the sum of the remaining half, and the game continues on that half, so if `leftSum < rightSum` Alice gets `leftSum + dp[left][mid]`, if `leftSum > rightSum` she gets `rightSum + dp[mid + 1][right]`, and if the sums are **equal** Alice may keep whichever half is better for her, so both options are considered. The best split is kept in `dp[left][right]`, and the final answer is `dp[0][n - 1]`, the best score over the whole row, running in **O(n³)** time with **O(n²)** space.
